title: Sky Signal Relay
premise: A futuristic sky-beacon operator fires colored signal orbs into a suspended cloud grid, clearing matching clusters before storm interference pushes the field too low.
interaction_model: Single-screen drag-to-aim and release-to-shoot arcade puzzle play with mouse and touch support, side-wall rebounds, and immediate score feedback.
objective: Shoot colored orbs to make groups of three or more matching colors, clear detached clusters for bonus points, and survive as long as possible without the stack reaching the lower fail zone.
progression: The board starts partially filled, each shot can either clear groups or worsen congestion, full clears instantly restart a fresh round, and the main progression loop is endless score chasing with repeated survival attempts.
theme: Sci-fi aurora relay station with beacon-grid language, storm interference framing, glowing signal colors, and atmospheric sky visuals.
mood: Bright, reactive, lightly tense, and arcade-like, with celebratory combo feedback and warning cues when the grid gets dangerously low.
likely_audience: fans of classic bubble shooter mechanics
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core design is a bubble-shooter / match-and-pop arcade puzzle because the code explicitly implements upward aiming, wall bounces, grid snapping, contiguous color matching, and floating-cluster drops.
Medium confidence on deeper fiction and worldbuilding because the relay narrative is mostly conveyed through title text, UI copy, and visual styling rather than systemic narrative content.
High confidence that the game is intended to be playable on both desktop and mobile due to touch listeners, viewport settings, and safe-area-aware UI.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen browser arcade puzzle game called "Sky Signal Relay" where the player controls a bottom-center launcher and clears a hanging field of colored signal orbs by dragging to aim and releasing to fire upward. The core play should feel like a classic bubble shooter: shots can bank off the left and right walls, the projectile snaps into the nearest slot on a staggered hex-style grid, and any connected group of 3 or more matching colors pops immediately. After each pop, detect clusters that are no longer connected to the top row and drop them for bonus points. Start each round with roughly five partially filled rows, keep the action score-driven and survival-based, and trigger game over when newly placed orbs reach a danger band near the bottom of the visible grid. If the player clears the whole field, instantly roll into a fresh round so the game loops endlessly for score chasing. Present it with a futuristic aurora-station theme: dark night-sky gradients, glowing cyan UI accents, a subtle atmospheric city-or-sky backdrop, luminous colored orb highlights, and menu text that frames the playfield as a beacon relay under storm interference. Include a start screen, a game-over overlay with final score, a visible HUD score counter, drag aim guide, pop particles, celebratory combo feedback for large matches or dropped clusters, warning feedback when the stack gets low, looping background music, reactive sound effects, and a mute toggle. Keep controls simple, readable, and mobile-safe.
